title: Align client-side call pacing, hedged-orchestration, and idempotency metadata for multi-region failover
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Different services and client SDKs use inconsistent call pacing, backoff curves, and hedged-request orchestration. This leads to burst amplification during regional failover, violating per-route SLOs and causing cascading circuit-breaker trips. Goal: Define and implement a standardized client-side pacing and hedging contract with bindable idempotency metadata, so services can safely execute hedged requests across regions while preserving SLOs and minimizing failover amplification.
context: We currently observe: - Region failover tests produce 2–3x peak RPS to secondary regions for a narrow window, exceeding latency SLOs. - SDKs implement ad-hoc backoffs (linear, exponential, jitter variants) with different default maxima. - Some services accept hedged requests without explicit idempotency keys, causing duplicate side effects. - Circuit breakers kick in at downstream services due to simultaneous hedges and retries leading to client-side fan-out. This ticket formalizes a contract that ties: per-route SLO targets, a pacing governor, hedging eligibility rules, idempotency metadata propagation, and circuit-breaker compatibility.
proposed_solution: 1) Define a compact client-side pacing governor API that exposes: target_qps, burst_budget, smoothing_window_ms, and max_concurrent_hedges per route. 2) Standardize a backoff curve family: SLO-aware backoff where initial retry delay is derived from the route latency P95 and scaled by a tunable factor. Provide reference algorithms for exponential-with-jitter and capped-linear variations. 3) Introduce 'idempotency_context' header schema: idempotency_key, idempotency_ttl_ms, operation_semantics (safe|unsafe|compensating). 4) Hedging orchestration rules: eligibility flags per route, max hedged replicas, hedged offset formula (fraction of route SLO minus p95 margin), and explicit bailout to prevent hedged fan-out. 5) Circuit-breaker handshake: clients should annotate hedged calls with circuit-breaker-intent so downstream breakers prioritize hedged traffic differently (e.g., treat hedged replicas as best-effort). 6) Provide SDK reference implementations (Go, Python, JS) plus runtime compatibility layer to translate legacy flags.
acceptance_criteria: SDK reference implementations in go-sdk, py-sdk, js-sdk with feature flags and unit tests
Chaos test: simulated region failover must not exceed a 20% QPS spike to secondaries for more than 30s compared to baseline
No increase in production duplicate-side-effect incidents during canary rollout (tracked by dedupe metrics)
Per-route SLO dashboards show stable P95/P99 during staged rollout
Runbook updated and on-call trained for hedged-failover scenarios
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Spec review and RFC (2 weeks). Phase 2: Implement SDK changes behind feature flags + internal integration tests (3 weeks). Phase 3: Canary on low-risk routes with monitoring and automated rollback (2 weeks). Phase 4: Gradual enablement by traffic class (critical -> high -> normal) and full rollout to runtime-1.24 (2 weeks). Each phase gated by automated chaos experiments and SLO checks.
testing_plan: Unit tests for pacing governor and idempotency header parsing. Integration tests: synthetic multi-region failover harness that measures peak amplification, p95, and dedupe counts. Chaos experiments: random region outage, network partition, and slow downstream dependencies. Load tests: validate burst_budget and hedged offset formulas under 0.1–10k RPS ranges.
monitoring_playbook: New metrics: client.pacing.target_qps, client.pacing.actual_qps, client.hedge.count, idempotency.duplicates, hedged_amplification_ratio. Dashboards: per-route SLO heatmap, hedged_fanout_alert. Alerts: hedged_amplification_ratio > 1.5 for > 60s, idempotency.duplicates rate increase > 2x baseline. Runbook steps include immediate rollback of SDK feature flag, circuit-breaker parameter adjustments, and coordinated region throttling.
